_readme: ONE FILE PER TRIP. Everything a trip needs: manifest, locations, itineraries. Drop a new file into public/trips/ and add it to index.json to publish it. See TRIP_SCHEMA.md for the authoring contract.
title: Japon & Hong Kong
subtitle: Three weeks at peak autumn

map._canvasNote: All trips in this project share one canvas ratio. The artwork carries its own margin so land never reaches the edge, and leaves clear space at the bottom for the dataviz. baseSize MUST match the real pixel size of base.
map._pathNote: All paths here are relative to this file's folder.
map._wavesNote: PARKED. Move entries from _wavesParked back into waves to turn them on. x/y are fractions of the map image, same space as pin coordinates — drag them in the CALIBRATE panel.
map._cloudsNote: Weather over the whole viewport, not features of the map: x/y and travel are percentages of the SCREEN, while size stays proportional to the map. x + travel must exceed 100 or the loop reset becomes visible.
map._calibratedNote: Placed by hand in the CALIBRATE panel against the 3840x2760 artwork, so these are measured rather than derived. x/y are fractions of the map image; the Hong Kong pin is a fraction of the inset box instead.

fonts._readme: Loaded on demand — only the trip being viewed fetches its faces. `google` is a Google Fonts family+axis string; `src` is a self-hosted file under public/. `fallback` is what shows while the face loads.

display._note: no CJK glyphs — kanji fall through to the fallback

ui._note: Optional 9-slice frames for the itinerary selector, in this trip's own folder because they are its art direction, not the product's. Omit them and the selector falls back to a flat plate in artDirection.colors — see --sel-panel-img in styles/main.css.

grid._source: Figma artboard 1920, count 8, type stretch, margin 218, gutter 20

budget._readme:
The footer's cost model. Three levers, each a real choice about THIS trip.
  sleep      not a lever in the data — it picks the cheapest / middle / dearest
             stay at each stop, so the figure is the actual sum of real hotels
  eat/move   per-trip bands, because a konbini breakfast in Japan is not a
             konbini breakfast in Portugal
Flights and activities are fixed: flights aren't optional, and activities only
swing a few hundred against a few thousand.

options.label: shinkansen where it saves a day

cta.headline: So… are you in?

flightSearch._readme: Every flight in the trip, in order. `mode` controls how they're offered: 'multiCity' builds one search across all legs (Kayak/Momondo only), 'perLeg' renders one link per leg. 'both' shows the combined search with per-leg links beneath, which is the safest default since a multi-city URL can't be verified without opening it.
flightSearch._legsNote: Legs live on each ITINERARY (itineraries[].flightSearch.legs), because only the first and last follow the itinerary dates — a shared list with hardcoded middle legs produced an impossible sequence the moment you switched duration. A trip-level `legs` here would still work as a fallback for an itinerary that defines none.
flightSearch._passengersNote: One ticket: the flights are booked and paid for separately. The ROOM is still for two — see cta.roomAdults.

cta._roomAdultsNote: How many share a room, used for the Booking.com links. Separate from flightSearch.passengers because you fly on your own tickets and share a twin.

locations.subtitle: Kowloon · HK Island · Lantau
locations.intro: We kick off in high gear. Bamboo steamers at midnight, glowing canyon streets, and Victoria Peak at dusk as the harbour explodes into neon. The perfect hyper-sensory jolt before the mountain silence.
locations.chipCaption: A neon cocktail of steam & concrete

thingsToDo.title: Dragon's Back ridge at sunrise
thingsToDo.note: Free. Bus there, noodles at the bottom.

thingsToDo.title: Star Ferry crossings
thingsToDo.note: Cheapest harbour view in the world.

thingsToDo.title: Sham Shui Po lanes and market stalls
thingsToDo.note: Free to wander; bring cash for snacks.

thingsToDo.title: Dim sum crawl
thingsToDo.note: Seafood and chicken baskets — skip the char siu.

locations.foodNotes: No char siu or pork buns — seafood and chicken dim sum are the safe defaults.
locations._photosNote: Beauty shots of the place, 1 to 6. They fill the slots of the layout named by `scatter` (0-3, see src/js/scatter.js) in order, so three photos use the first three positions. All 1000px tall with whatever width they came with — the card crops nothing.
locations._staysNote: A stay with isArea:true is a KIND of place in an area, not a named property — its link searches the area rather than a hotel that doesn't exist. Replace the name with a real property and drop isArea when you find one.

locations.subtitle: Takayama · Kamikochi · Shin-Hotaka
locations.intro: This is where we go offline. Six nights trekking alpine trails framed by peak autumn larches, staying in historic wooden towns, and sinking into steaming outdoor onsen beneath cold starlit skies.

thingsToDo.title: Kamikochi at dawn — Taisho Pond mirror-still
thingsToDo.note: Bus in; private cars are banned.

thingsToDo.title: Shin-Hotaka Ropeway
thingsToDo.note: Double-decker cable car, return fare.

thingsToDo.title: Shirakawa-go thatched village
thingsToDo.note: Nohi bus return from Takayama.

thingsToDo.title: Takayama morning market + Hida beef
thingsToDo.note: Skewers at the market, or a proper sit-down.

locations.foodNotes: Hida beef is the regional specialty — beef, not pork, so an easy no-pork base.

locations.subtitle: Kenroku-en · Higashi Chaya · Omicho
locations.intro: A castle town that was never bombed, so it was never rebuilt. Gold-leaf workshops, black-tile roofs, and teahouse lanes that light from the inside at dusk.

thingsToDo.title: Kenroku-en Garden at opening time
thingsToDo.note: Go before the tour groups.

thingsToDo.title: Higashi Chaya geisha district
thingsToDo.note: Free to walk; teahouse entry extra.

thingsToDo.title: Omicho Market seafood lunch
thingsToDo.note: Kaisendon at the counter.

thingsToDo.title: Gold-leaf workshop
thingsToDo.note: Make something to take home.

locations.foodNotes: Kaiseki dinners — flag no-pork when booking.

locations.subtitle: Wakura Onsen · Nanao
locations.intro: A day out to a coastline still finding its feet after 2024. Terraced rice fields running straight into the sea, and almost nobody else on the train.
locations.chipCaption: A coast that went quiet again

thingsToDo.title: Wakura Onsen day bath
thingsToDo.note: Public bath at the hot spring town.

thingsToDo.title: Nanao coastline by local train
thingsToDo.note: Return fare from Kanazawa.

locations.subtitle: Ohara · Kurama · Arashiyama
locations.intro: Kyoto without the crush. We stay on the edges and head up into the hills instead — moss temples in Ohara, cedar forest above Kurama, bamboo at first light.

thingsToDo.title: Sanzen-in Temple, Ohara
thingsToDo.note: Moss gardens, mountain village quiet.

thingsToDo.title: Kurama–Kibune cedar walk
thingsToDo.note: Trail fee plus optional cable car.

thingsToDo.title: Arashiyama bamboo at first light
thingsToDo.note: Free — but be there before 7am.

thingsToDo.title: Adashino Nenbutsu-ji stone statues
thingsToDo.note: Thousands of them, almost no one there.

locations.foodNotes: Shojin ryori (temple vegetarian) is a naturally no-pork option here.

locations.subtitle: Tottori Dunes · Mt. Daisen
locations.intro: Japan's least-visited coastline. Sand dunes on one side, the west's answer to Fuji on the other, reflected in a pond most people have never heard of.

thingsToDo.title: Tottori Sand Dunes
thingsToDo.note: Free; sandboard or camel ride extra.

thingsToDo.title: Mt. Daisen + Kagamigaike pond
thingsToDo.note: Free trail; Daisen-ji donation.

thingsToDo.title: Sand Museum
thingsToDo.note: Sculpture, surprisingly good.

locations.subtitle: Chichu · Benesse · Art House Project
locations.intro: An art island where we sleep inside the museum. Guests get the galleries after the day-trippers leave — the one night worth breaking the budget for.

thingsToDo.title: Chichu Art Museum
thingsToDo.note: Book ahead — timed entry.

thingsToDo.title: Benesse House museum
thingsToDo.note: Free if you're staying the night.

thingsToDo.title: Art House Project
thingsToDo.note: Multi-site ticket through the village.

locations.subtitle: Onomichi · Imabari · the islands
locations.intro: Seventy kilometres of bridges island-hopping across the Inland Sea on rented bikes, citrus groves and fishing harbours on both sides.

thingsToDo.title: Shimanami Kaido one-way bike rental
thingsToDo.note: Drop-off at the far end included.

thingsToDo.title: Bridge tolls
thingsToDo.note: A few hundred yen per bridge.

thingsToDo.title: Onomichi temple walk
thingsToDo.note: Free; ropeway up is extra.

locations.subtitle: Ryogoku · Meiji Jingu Gaien · Shibuya
locations.intro: Two nights to land back on earth, starting at 7am on a tatami floor two metres from a sumo ring. Then golden ginkgo avenues and one last stretch of shopping.

thingsToDo.title: Sumo stable morning practice
thingsToDo.note: Small group, must be arranged ahead.

thingsToDo.title: Meiji Jingu Gaien ginkgo avenue
thingsToDo.note: Free, and peaking exactly then.

thingsToDo.title: Depachika food halls
thingsToDo.note: Last meals and gifts.

locations.subtitle: Danjo Garan · Okunoin · Shukubo
locations.intro: A working Buddhist monastery town founded by Kukai in 816, thick with cedar and incense smoke. We sleep inside a temple, eat what the monks eat, and walk into the largest cemetery in Japan at dusk with a single lantern.

thingsToDo.title: Okunoin cemetery night walk
thingsToDo.note: Guided lantern walk through 200,000 graves.

thingsToDo.title: Danjo Garan & Konpon Daito pagoda
thingsToDo.note: The vermillion heart of the complex.

thingsToDo.title: Morning goma fire ritual
thingsToDo.note: Included with any shukubo stay.

thingsToDo.title: Daimon Gate & cable car arrival
thingsToDo.note: The dramatic way in, via Nankai Koya Line.

locations.foodNotes: Shojin ryori (Buddhist vegetarian) comes with every shukubo stay — naturally meat-free, zero pork risk.

locations.subtitle: Yunomine Onsen · Hongu Taisha · Nakahechi
locations.intro: A thousand-year-old pilgrimage route through cedar-dark mountains to three Grand Shrines, ending most days in a hot spring older than the trail itself. This is where the trip goes fully offline.

thingsToDo.title: Nakahechi trail day-hikes
thingsToDo.note: Takijiri to Chikatsuyu to Hongu, in stages.

thingsToDo.title: Kumano Hongu Taisha
thingsToDo.note: One of three Grand Shrines, free to enter.

thingsToDo.title: Tsuboyu bath, Yunomine Onsen
thingsToDo.note: The only UNESCO-listed bath you can actually bathe in.

thingsToDo.title: Luggage forwarding between inns
thingsToDo.note: Takkyubin courier — book through your minshuku.

locations.foodNotes: Minshuku dinners are river-fish and mountain-vegetable based — an easy no-pork base, but flag ahead at smaller family-run inns.

locations.subtitle: Nachi Taisha · Seiganto-ji · Japan's tallest waterfall
locations.intro: A single 133-metre drop, worshipped as a kami in its own right, with a vermillion pagoda framed against it. A short detour off the Kumano trail that punches far above its weight.

thingsToDo.title: Nachi Falls viewing platform
thingsToDo.note: Free view; closer platform is a small fee.

thingsToDo.title: Kumano Nachi Taisha & Seiganto-ji
thingsToDo.note: Shrine and pagoda side by side on the hillside.

thingsToDo.title: Daimonzaka stone stairway walk
thingsToDo.note: Mossy cedar-lined approach, free.

locations.foodNotes: Katsuura is a major tuna port — fresh maguro sashimi is the local specialty.

locations.subtitle: Dotonbori · Kuromon Market · Osaka Castle
locations.intro: Two loud, greasy, glorious days back among people after the mountain quiet — kuidaore, 'eat till you drop,' is Osaka's actual civic motto, and we take it seriously before the flight home.

thingsToDo.title: Dotonbori street food crawl
thingsToDo.note: Takoyaki, okonomiyaki, kushikatsu under the neon.

thingsToDo.title: Kuromon Ichiba Market
thingsToDo.note: Breakfast among the stalls.

thingsToDo.title: Osaka Castle grounds & keep
thingsToDo.note: Grounds free, keep entry is separate.

thingsToDo.title: Umeda Sky Building observation deck
thingsToDo.note: Best skyline view at sunset.

locations.foodNotes: Kushikatsu stalls fry pork by default — ask for chicken or vegetable skewers to avoid it.

itineraries.label: Alps & Inland Sea
itineraries._flightsNote: Paris→Hong Kong, Hong Kong→Nagoya, Okayama→Tokyo. The Tokyo→Paris return is treated as going home rather than a trip leg — change to 4 if you'd rather count it.

pitch._note: The argument for THIS itinerary — three stacked slides between the map and the dataviz. Not a highlight reel: mood sets the feeling, arguments makes exactly three distinct claims (not the same point three ways), gem is ONE vivid moment, held singular on purpose. Numbers describing the EXPERIENCE stay ('seventy kilometres of bridges'); numbers describing the ITINERARY go (nights, days, stop counts) — those read as a schedule, not a story, and belong on the map and in the popover instead.

mood.headline: The colour is moving south with you.
mood.body: Larches turning gold in the mountains, then ginkgo lighting up gold in Tokyo by the time you get there. You're not visiting in autumn — you're chasing the same wave of colour down the country.

arguments.headline: Hong Kong isn't a stopover.
arguments.body: It's a country in its own right, before Japan even starts.

arguments.headline: There's a stretch of this with no signal at all.
arguments.body: Alpine trail, hot water, cold stars — nothing scheduled, nothing to check.

arguments.headline: Built to dodge the queue, not join it.
arguments.body: A castle town never rebuilt. A coastline still finding its feet after 2024, with almost nobody on the train.

gem.headline: You cross the sea on a bicycle.
gem.body: Seventy kilometres of bridges, island to island across the Inland Sea — citrus groves and fishing harbours passing on both sides, salt air the whole way.

flightSearch._note: Four legs. If the Kayak link fails to resolve, the domestic OKJ→TYO hop is the one to drop — it is a cheap short flight you would book separately anyway, and removing it leaves a clean 3-leg open jaw (PAR→HKG, HKG→NGO, TYO→PAR) that matches the shape of the other two itineraries.

itineraries.label: Temples & Trails
itineraries._flightsNote: Paris→Hong Kong, Hong Kong→Kansai (Osaka), transferring up to Koyasan by rail. The return flight departs Kansai Airport itself, so it's treated as going home rather than a trip leg.

itineraries.label: Coast & Islands
itineraries._flightsNote: Inbound flight connecting to Kanazawa (via Komatsu or Osaka with an onward transfer), then Hiroshima/Okayama→Tokyo for the last leg. The Tokyo→home return is treated as going home rather than a trip leg.
itineraries._mapNote: Optional per-itinerary artwork. Same dimensions as map.base, so pins, crop and inset stay valid; the two are crossfaded. Uncomment when the asset exists: "map": { "base": "map-coast.png" }

flightSearch._note: No Hong Kong on this one, and Okayama→Tokyo is a surface leg here — so it is an open jaw: into Komatsu for Kanazawa, home from Tokyo.
